Children of affairs

A married noblewoman in an affair may bear her lover's child (5% a week the two are together). The game counts her husband as the father, so the child is legitimate and no succession changes; the truth is a secret of the mother and the lover, whispered about if the affair comes to light. Never your own heirs.
Also unmarried mothers

An unmarried noblewoman in an affair may bear her lover's child too. The child is then the lover's in the game, born into the lover's house: illegitimate with Bellum Civile 1.4.3 or later (out of the succession and the inheritance), able to inherit there otherwise. It cannot be hidden: at the birth the affair comes to light. Off by default.
Chance to conceive a week together (%)
The chance each week the lovers are together (same castle or town, party or army) that a child is conceived, with children of affairs on. Default 5.
How long affairs last (%)
How long an affair goes on before it is broken off or comes to light: 200 about twice as long, 50 about half. At 100 most last a season or two.
Nobles have affairs (experimental)

A noble in an unhappy marriage (no pull toward their own spouse) and someone they want, who wants them back, may become lovers in secret. It takes rapport (or a feeling that lingers from before a marriage), and being close lately; honour holds them back: an honourable noble needs more of everything (rapport 70 with Honor 1, 90 with Honor 2; a stronger pull; closer lately). Rulers and their families too; never you (your family and companions, yes); a realm with one going on is half as likely to see another. It is broken off, or it comes to light, likelier the longer it lasts, or when word of it reaches the spouse. A noble of a strict culture (Calradia Remembers' jealousy cultures: Vlandia, the Empire, Sturgia) strays half as often. The wronged spouse forgives if generous or merciful (more readily in a lenient culture, and bears it where their people accept a shared partner); otherwise holds a grudge against the lover (a feud, if they speak for their house) and against their spouse, heavier in a strict culture. All of it remembered in Calradia Remembers. Runs rapport even with attachments off. Off by itself when Dramalord is loaded.
New affairs per year (world)
A ceiling: at most this many new affairs a year, in the whole world. A realm with one going on is half as likely to see another.
Lovers while fond of another
On: a noble fond of someone may still take a lover nearby, carrying the flame for the other. Off: someone fond of another takes no lover.
Nobles grow fond of each other (experimental)

Two unmarried nobles who have lived through things together (battles, an army, grief, a tournament) may grow fond of each other, if they feel the pull: like values attract, opposite ones only between respectful rivals (the lists, opposite sides at court in Bellum Civile); looks (weight and build, to each one's taste) and admiration (glory, prowess, charm, power, fame or friends, whichever each values) add to it; ill will shuts it. Mutual, or one of them in secret. They remember it in Calradia Remembers. It marries nobody and changes no house: it ends when one of them marries (the feeling lingers, from one year to ten with the rapport), dies, or after two years. Off by itself when Dramalord is loaded.
New attachments per year (world)
A ceiling: at most this many new attachments a campaign year, in the whole world.
Children born out of wedlock are looked down on

A child born out of wedlock (illegitimate in Bellum Civile 1.4.3, which includes your own when Bridges to Remember marks them, or born of an affair to an unmarried mother) is looked down on: a lasting leaning that relations drift toward, -20 where customs are strict, -10 middling, -5 lenient, nothing where houses share partners. Never by their own parents, siblings or spouse. It ends when they are legitimized. Shown in the Relation tooltip.
How heavily (%)
How heavily a birth out of wedlock weighs, in percent of -20 strict / -10 middling / -5 lenient. 50 halves it, 200 doubles it.
Lords remember who beat whom

Every lord's battles against you are counted. At the 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 8th, 12th and 20th time you beat them they remember it in their own temper (the brave want the next fight, the cautious would rather not meet you, the rest respect you); a lord who beats you remembers the 1st, 3rd and 5th time, and paying you back after losing twice or more. Off: no such memories. Without Calradia Remembers they are kept in the encyclopedia, under the relation on their page.
Battles bind those of a like temper more

Rapport from a battle on the same side weighs temper: +1 for each of Valor, Honor, Mercy and Calculating the two hold alike, -1 for each opposed, never under +1. Off: every battle gives the same (+3, +4 in a defeat).
Between NPCs too (experimental)

On: every pair of nobles has a relation of their own, not only with you, starting from what their clan leaders think of each other. Off: as in the base game, two NPCs share their clan leaders' relation. Turning it off keeps what they had; it comes back when turned on again. With Bellum Civile, turn off its Enable Relationship Memory.
Quarrels in your camp (Affairs of Calradia)

With Affairs of Calradia: its notes from your camp leave something. Two companions who argued by the fire: rapport +1 and rivals (their differences pull for a while). Who came to blows: rivals and +0.5, or a grudge of 8 each way if they were on bad terms already. One who settled a quarrel among the men: rapport +1 with you. They remember it. The other notes (training, hunting, drinking, prayer...) are left alone. Off: the notes leave nothing.
Castle knights (Realistic Medieval Castles)

With Realistic Medieval Castles: the two knights of each castle count like nobles for rapport: days in their castle with those there, serving its lord (a little each day), your drills in its courtyard (+1 to +4 with you, +1 between the two). When the castle changes hands they remember it, and may resent a lord who took it by siege from one they were bound to. In Calradia Remembers they are told whom they serve and how bound they are. Off: left out, as before.
Clear the game's random starting friendships

On: on a new campaign, the friendships and enmities the game hands out at random between lords (a lady of the Empire, close friends with a Khuzait she has never met) are cleared in its first hours. Two lords of different clans who are not kin start at 0, or at their leaning with the option above. Kin keep theirs. A campaign already under way is never touched.
Companion patrols (Calradia Remembers)

With Calradia Remembers 2.7.15 or later: a companion you send on patrol around a place. The lord who holds it (not you, not at war with you): +1 for each fight the patrol wins, at most 3, and he remembers it. When it is over the companion remembers it and gains rapport with you (after 7 days out), and the place's notables remember it if a fight was won. Off: patrols leave nothing.
Standing per regard lost
Each point of regard lost takes away this much relation. 0: losing regard never costs standing.
Relation lost by their family

How much relation the family of the one left behind (their kin who are not the lovers' kin, and the heads of their house and of the house they were born to) loses with both lovers, and the weight of their grudges. Default 60.
Relation lost by the one left behind

How much relation the one left behind loses with both lovers, and the weight of the grudge they hold against each. Where two keep no relation of their own it falls on their houses' heads, as in the game. Default 100.
Lovers run off together (experimental)

Lovers who cannot give each other up may run off together: an affair never found out, of 50 days or more with rapport 80 or more (75 days and 90 when either is honourable), and Valor in one of them. The one who is married leaves their spouse, and the two are wed by the game's own wedding, which chooses their house; children stay where they are. The scandal follows, as when an affair comes to light. Never a ruler, never your clan or your spouse. The one left behind and their family never forgive it: the relations below, and grudges that never wear off (a feud, if they speak for their house). Two unmarried courting without consent (their houses at odds, or your blessing refused) may run off too: courting 50 days, rapport 60 (75 days and 80 when honourable), Valor in one; never into your clan against your word; the head of a house one of them left never forgives it (the family relation below). Affairs on for the first, courtships for the second.
Elopements per year (world)
A ceiling: at most this many lovers run off together a year, in the whole world.
Exact numbers (no Charm)
On: exactly the numbers above. Off: your Charm skill and perks grow gains, as the game does for every relation gain (in testing, +3 became +6).
Your relations fade over time
Good relations never fade below
An old friend stays at least this friendly. 0: everything fades toward 0.
Grudges fade too
On: bad relations also drift back toward 0. Off: they stay until you mend them.

Your relations drift slowly toward 0 unless something keeps them up (talking, quests, battles...), so you are not at 100 with everyone forever. Only relations with you: relations between NPCs and your own clan are never touched. With Bellum Civile's Relationship Memory on (its default), the lords and notables it manages are left to it, since it already fades them; this then covers everyone else. Do not combine with another mod that fades relations, such as Calradia Forgets, or they will fade twice.
Points lost per year
How fast, per year of 84 days (the normal year; rate_year_days in the file), so fast mode keeps the same pace per day. 6 takes 100 down to about 64 in six years.
Talking holds off fading (days)
After a Calradia Remembers chat in which you said something, that person's relation with you does not fade for this many days: keeping in touch keeps a relation up. 0: chats do not count.
Feasts bind those who attend (Convivium)

With Convivium: Living Feasts: nobles who attended the same feast (12 hours or more in its settlement) get rapport +4 with each other and +2 more with the host, like a wedding between two houses. Without Bridges to Remember each also remembers the feast. Off: feasts give nothing. Turn off Convivium's own courtship, pregnancy and scandals in its menu so two systems do not do the same thing.
Fond of how many at once
How many nobles one may be fond of at the same time, each fondness a story of its own. 1: one at a time, as before.
Affairs between NPCs
Attachments between NPCs
Grudges between NPCs
Natural leanings
Own relations
Regard and Standing
The matchmaker
Kin killed in battle leave a grudge
On: a noble holds a grudge against whoever killed their kin in battle. Off: only murders and executions do, for mods where far more lords die in battle (Death for All).
Weight for a feud between houses
A grudge this heavy becomes a feud between the houses (once). A murdered father is 35, an executed one 30, one killed in battle 12; grudges add up.
Grudges fade per year
Points a grudge loses each campaign year. 0: they never fade.
Nobles hold grudges (experimental)

Nobles hold grudges against each other: for kin killed (murdered, executed, in battle) or for marrying someone they were fond of. They remember it privately in Calradia Remembers, and it wears off with time. A strong one held by a house's leader, or their spouse or close kin, becomes a feud between the two houses: their leaders' relation drops and the word goes around. Never yours: Calradia Remembers keeps those.
Word spreads person to person

On: word of an attachment or a feud spreads from person to person (same party, army, town, family). Those it touches personally (kin, the one a secret is about) remember it in Calradia Remembers; the world hears it once in Calradia Remembers' news, so it never crowds out anyone's memories. A secret fondness can slip out, and the one it is about may hear of it. Off: only the court-wide rumor.
Debts of honor

Only the extraordinary counts. Free a noble of another realm, not at war with you (from a dungeon, or from captors after a day or more), or let an enemy noble you hold go without ransom, and they, their spouse, parents, children, siblings and the head of their house owe you a debt of honor; free one of your own realm and only their close kin do (to them it was what a fellow lord does). Not friendship: an obligation between nobles, told in every prompt with Calradia Remembers, and it stands even if you wrong them later. It does not fade; it is paid only in kind: they let you or one of yours go while at war with you, rescue you from another realm, or rescue one of your house. Off: no such debts.
Include children
Off: children keep their clan leader's relation until they come of age, and only then get one of their own.
Include minor clans and mercenaries
Off: only the realms' noble clans. Minor clans and mercenary companies keep the game's clan-leader rule.
Most chance of an invitation (%)
The chance is your tournament wins / 4 + your level / 4 + your clan's tier x 2 + his relation / 15, less 2 for each invitation open, and never more than this.
Days to answer
An invitation unanswered for this many days lapses, without a word and without a penalty.
Invitations come as the host's letter (Calradia Remembers)

With Calradia Remembers 2.7.17 or later: the invitation is the host's letter, carried by its courier, opened in its letter window and kept in its letter book; he remembers writing it. The notice beside the map still asks accept or decline. Off: the whole letter is in the notice.
Farthest invitation (days' ride)

An invitation comes only from a tournament you can reach before it ends (the game ends it about 15 days after it begins), and no farther than this many days' ride from where you are. The invitation says how many days it has left and how far it is.
Invitations open at once
No new invitation while this many are open (unanswered, or accepted and not yet held).
Families remember their dead

When someone dies, their spouse, parents, children and siblings remember it, with the full name, what the dead was to them and how they died: "My daughter Debana the Lioness died in childbirth." When one of your spouses dies, your other spouses remember it too (with Affairs of Calradia's polygamy as well). A violent death reaches the rest of the house too: for an execution or a murder its head and adult nobles (eight at most), for a death in battle its head ("Siga, of our house, was executed by order of X."). An execution at your hand is left to Calradia Remembers for the close kin, which already tells the kin. Off: no such memories. Without Calradia Remembers they are kept in the encyclopedia.
Share that reaches the clan leader

With own relations on, a clan member's change lands on them alone; this part of it also reaches their clan leader, from regard or from the game itself (freeing him after a battle, a quest, a raid). 0.25: a quarter. 0: the leader never hears of it.
Relations drift toward their natural leaning (experimental)

Each pair has a natural leaning: what kinship, character, culture and the realms would make of the two (with Bellum Civile, its politics too). See it by hovering over Relation on a hero's encyclopedia page. On: relations drift slowly toward it: yours with each noble, every pair of clan leaders, and the NPC pairs that have their own. It replaces fading. Clan leaders' relations with their ruler are what Bellum Civile weighs for rebellions. With Bellum's Relationship Memory on, the pairs it manages are left to it.
Points per year toward the leaning
How fast a relation moves toward its leaning, per year of 84 days (the normal year; rate_year_days in the file). It never goes past it.
NPC relations start from their leaning (experimental)

On: once per campaign, each pair of clan leaders gets its leaning added to what the game gave it; a new leader later starts at the leaning. With 'Between NPCs too', each new NPC pair starts at its leaning instead of a share of their leaders'. Your own relations keep their start. Best on a new campaign.
Longest a feeling lingers (years)

When the beloved marries another, the feeling lingers: from one year (a summer fling) up to this many (true love). By the rapport, up to this less two; a year more for an honourable heart, and a year more if the fondness had lasted a year or more. While it lingers it can turn into an affair.
Your clan asks your blessing

One of your clan (family or companion) who courts someone, after a fortnight, asks for your blessing with a notice beside the map. Given, they wed at once, by the game's own wedding; a companion, whom the game does not count as a noble, becomes a noble of your house at the wedding. Refused, they remember it, and daring lovers may run off anyway, out of your clan, never into it. Dismissed unanswered, they ask again after a season. Off: your clan is left out of courtships, as before.
Houses agree from (relation)

Below this relation between the heads of two houses, they do not agree to a wedding between them: the couple courts and waits, or may run off. Default -20 (the game itself allows down to -50); Maifailun's idea was 0.
Courtship and marriage (experimental)

Two nobles fond of each other, both ways, for a season, with rapport 40 or more, may start courting, and then marry through the game's own wedding (its rules of age, clan and house; Calradia Remembers records it). Not without consent: the heads of their houses at odds, or, for one of your clan, your blessing. Not when their realms are at war; never a ruler. Without consent they court and wait, or may run off (affairs group). Needs attachments on.
Weddings per year (world)
A ceiling: at most this many weddings out of courtship a year, in the whole world.
Your family proposes matches
Most years apart
A match is proposed only within this many years of age.
Other houses ask you for a match

Once a month at most, the head of a house on good terms with you (relation 10 or more) asks whom of your family you would see their unmarried son or daughter marry. Name one, or no one; naming one gives the two a little rapport and the head remembers your answer. Nobody is promised.
Days between proposals (0: a year)
How often each unmarried member gets new proposals. 0: once a game year. One notice a week at most.

Maifailun's idea: the eldest of your family proposes three matches for an unmarried member of your clan, one they already get on with, one of a house on good terms with you, one of a strong house, and says which they would choose. A notice beside the map; choosing one gives the two a little rapport. Only a suggestion: nobody is married or promised; the wedding is yours to arrange, as before.
For you too
While you are unmarried, your family proposes matches for you as well (your chamberlain, if you have no elder family).
Most the game adds at once

The most the game itself adds to your relation with someone at once, after Charm. Some of the game's sums run away: a lord freed after a battle once thanked you with +90. Only gains with you; losses and regard are not touched. 0: no ceiling.
Most standing per regard change
The most relation a single regard change can move, either way. 0: no cap. 10 keeps a quest worth +10 regard from moving standing by 30.
Regard moves standing
Personal regard won or lost in Calradia Remembers also moves the game's own relation (clan standing). Off: the two stay apart, as in Calradia Remembers alone.
Tell: courtships and weddings
Two nobles courting, and the wedding a courtship ends in. Off: neither notice nor message.
Tell: feuds between houses
A grudge become ill will between two houses. Off: neither notice nor message.
Tell: who has grown fond of whom
Two nobles fond of each other, as the court comes to know it. Off: neither notice nor message (Calradia Remembers still has it as news).
Court rumors on screen (without CR)

Without Calradia Remembers: who has grown fond of whom, a courtship, a scandal or a feud is shown on screen as a message as it becomes known at court, where Calradia Remembers would tell it as news. With Calradia Remembers this does nothing. Off: in the log only. The notice beside the map has its own switch below.
Tell: affairs found out and scandals
An affair whispered about or come to light, and whose child it may be. Off: neither notice nor message.
Court news as a notice beside the map

The court's news as a notice beside the map, like the game's own for a new season or a wedding, so it is not lost in a battle's log: hover for the text, click to read it and dismiss it. Without Calradia Remembers; with it, see the next switch. Not kept in the save: one left unread is gone after loading.
Notices with Calradia Remembers too
With Calradia Remembers its chat already tells these as news. On: the notices beside the map as well.
Show the relation notice
The game's usual 'relation increased' message when standing moves.
Friends and enemies in Calradia Remembers count this mod's reasons

With Calradia Remembers 2.7.17 or later: its own weighing of two people (a friend or an enemy in its chat and on the encyclopedia page) counts this mod's reasons too: a grudge (-5 to -30), rapport of 20 or more (+5 to +30), rivals in the lists (-5), a debt of honor owed to you (+15). Calradia Remembers caps all other mods together at 40 either way. Takes effect from the next campaign loaded. Off: it weighs only its own reasons.
Each noble has their own relation

Each noble has their own relation with you, not their clan leader's. Off: back to the game's rule, where the whole clan shares the leader's. Relations already given stay in the save and come back when you turn it on again. Using Affairs of Calradia's personal relations? Turn one of the two off.
Feelings toward you in every prompt (CR)

With Calradia Remembers: each character's rapport with you, romantic pull toward you, secret fondness and grudge, in numbers and in words, in every prompt ({{rs_toward_player}}), so the model weighs this mod's attraction and not only Calradia Remembers' regard. Off: only as memories, as before.
Rapport needed

Shared experience a pair needs before an attachment can start (up to 100): a battle side by side 3, a day in the same army 0.5, a tournament 2, grief over kin lost to the same house 10, a day in the same town 0.2 (10 at most), a captivity that ended well with a merciful or honourable captor 1 a day (15 at most). It wears off 3% a week. A pull is needed too: like values, or opposite ones between respectful rivals.
Year for rates and ceilings (days)

The year that rates and yearly ceilings are measured in: points a year (fading, leanings, grudges), new attachments and affairs a year, how fast an affair starts or comes to light. 84 is the game's normal year, so with a fast-mode calendar (shorter years) these keep the same pace per day. 0: everything follows the game's own year.
Regard sways persuasion (%)

Regard as a will to listen: a noble who holds you dear is easier to persuade in the game's persuasion screen (courting, convincing, quests), one who loathes you harder. The percent at full regard; 0: regard does not count.
Remember game changes of at least

A change of the game's own relation with you this big or more is remembered by that noble (in Calradia Remembers, or without it on their encyclopedia page), when its reason is known (Bellum Civile names it, or you helped them in battle). A battle's memory says where and how it went. 0: never. (Who beat whom has its own switch below.)
Shared past before the campaign (Calradia Remembers)

With Calradia Remembers 2.7.15 or later: what it draws two lords lived through before the campaign counts here too, once each. Old friends: rapport +15; rode together +8; a life saved +10; an insult never forgiven: a grudge of 12; a debt never repaid: 8; a quarrel over grazing land: 6 each way; a rivalry in the lists: rivals. Off: it is only told, as before.
Regard causes that never move standing

Calradia Remembers names each regard change by its cause: conversation, letter, quest, commitment, compensation, grudge, jealousy, divorce, rescue, stance, violence, departure, unspecified. Those listed here (separated by commas) never move your relation. Default: unspecified, divorce (Calradia Remembers already moves the relation itself for a divorce).
Starting enemies in a neighbouring realm

With the option above: each lord of a realm starts with this many enemies in a neighbouring realm, one whose castles and towns lie nearest theirs (-30 to -60), drawn anew for each campaign: a Vlandian lord may start with an enemy in Battania. 0: none.
Starting friends in their own realm

With the option above, in place of the game's random ties: each lord of a realm starts with this many friends among the other houses of their own realm (+30 to +60), drawn anew for each campaign. Never kin. 0: none.
Starting relation (% of clan leader's)

What each clan member starts with, as a share of their clan leader's relation with you. 100 copies it; 0 starts everyone from scratch. Only for those who do not have a relation of their own yet: changing it never touches anyone who already has one.
Old rivals (culture>culture)

Old rivals by the realms' cultures: "a>b" sends the starting enemies of a realm of culture a to a realm of culture b, however far, and lets b's lords draw theirs from a too. Culture ids or names (vlandia, empire, sturgia, battania, khuzait, aserai, nord, rhodok), separated by commas. Empty: neighbours only. Default: rhodok>vlandia.
Regard and Standing
Dedicate a victory

After you win a tournament, a line in the conversation with a lord of another house dedicates the victory to them, once per victory and within 30 days of it: +1 to +3, rapport +2, and they remember it.
Lords invite you to their tournaments

When a tournament starts, the lord of the town may invite you (idea from TripleThreat's Healthy Relationships): not in the first week, at peace with his realm, your crime there under 15, his relation with you -30 or better, outside an army. A notice beside the map: accept +1, decline -1 (your Charm may save you). Come +1 to +2, win +2 to +5 more; accept and never come -2 to -3, unless duty kept you (war between your realms, a new war, an army, a siege, captivity). He remembers it. War between your realms withdraws an open invitation. Never when a Convivium feast is held in that town.
Invitations touch the game's relation
Off: invitations and dedications give only rapport and memories, and the game's relation is left alone (for collections where another mod keeps it).
Trace on screen
Also print each mirrored change on screen. They are always in Documents\RegardStanding\regard_standing_log.txt. Which causes never count is set in regard_standing.txt (skip_causes).
Standing per regard gained
Each point of regard gained adds this much relation. 0.5: one point for every two of regard.
Vengeance oaths leave a grudge (Heroes Evolve)

With Heroes Evolve: a lord, or a companion riding for a house, stripped of his gear while a prisoner swears his house will pay it back. He holds a grudge of 20 against the one who stripped him (a companion never starts a feud), halved when his house has its vengeance. Read off the game's own log; Heroes Evolve is not touched. Off: the oaths plant nothing.
